name: ioat_dca_init
prose: Precondition: pdev is the ioat PCI device and iobase its mapped register base. Behaviour: it returns NULL if system_has_dca_enabled(pdev) is false, if the DCA offset register read is 0, or if ioat_dca_count_dca_slots finds no slots. It allocates a DCA provider sized for the slots with alloc_dca_provider (NULL on failure), fills in iobase, dca_base and max_requesters, and sets the CSI prefetch bit and PCIe memory-write bit in the DCA control registers by read-modify-write if they are clear. It reads the 64-bit APICID tag map, stores its eight bytes masked with DCA_TAG_MAP_MASK in the private data, and if dca3_tag_map_invalid reports the BIOS default map it taints the kernel (TAINT_FIRMWARE_WORKAROUND), warns once, frees the provider and returns NULL. Otherwise it calls register_dca_provider(dca, &pdev->dev); if that fails it frees the provider and returns NULL, and on success it returns the provider.
note: slice cut head; real name is ioat_dca_init (ioat/dca.c:249-333); no ioat3_dca_init exists in this tree. Old prose matches the code except it omitted the control-register writes.

name: src_cnt_flags
prose: Precondition: src_cnt and flags are plain integer arguments (the sum is computed in unsigned arithmetic and returned as int). Behaviour: a pure function. It returns src_cnt + 1 if both DMA_PREP_CONTINUE and DMA_PREP_PQ_DISABLE_P are set in flags (dmaf_p_disabled_continue), otherwise src_cnt + 3 if DMA_PREP_CONTINUE is set, otherwise src_cnt. It has no side effects.
note: prep.c:563-571; dmaf_continue and dmaf_p_disabled_continue at include/linux/dmaengine.h:1290-1300 test the flag bits by name. Contract left empty because the flag values are named constants not visible in the formula.

name: ioat_prep_pq
prose: Precondition: dst has at least two entries (written when the P or Q disable flag is set), src has src_cnt entries and scf src_cnt coefficient bytes. Behaviour: it returns NULL without touching dst if the channel has IOAT_CHAN_DOWN set. Otherwise it sets dst[0] = dst[1] if DMA_PREP_PQ_DISABLE_P is set and dst[1] = dst[0] if DMA_PREP_PQ_DISABLE_Q is set. If DMA_PREP_PQ_DISABLE_P is set and src_cnt is 1 it BUG_ONs when DMA_PREP_PQ_DISABLE_Q is also set, and builds a two-entry source list using src[0] twice with coefficients scf[0] and 0; in this and the normal case it returns the result of __ioat_prep_pq16_lock when src_cnt_flags(src_cnt, flags) is greater than 8 and of __ioat_prep_pq_lock otherwise. Those helpers return NULL when the ring has no space (the lock is released then), and the 16-source helper also returns NULL when no SED entry can be allocated, in which case it returns with the prep_lock still held; on success they return a descriptor with prep_lock left held to keep submission in order.
note: checked prep.c:573-616, 338-460, 462-561 and ioat_check_space_lock (dma.c:463-488). The old prose omitted that the SED-failure NULL return keeps prep_lock held (lines 505-511).

name: ioat_prep_pq_val
prose: Precondition: pq has at least two entries, src has src_cnt entries, scf has src_cnt coefficient bytes, pqres is writable. Behaviour: it returns NULL without touching pq or *pqres if the channel has IOAT_CHAN_DOWN set. Otherwise it sets pq[0] = pq[1] if DMA_PREP_PQ_DISABLE_P is set and pq[1] = pq[0] if DMA_PREP_PQ_DISABLE_Q is set, sets *pqres to 0, and returns the result of __ioat_prep_pq16_lock if src_cnt_flags(src_cnt, flags) > 8, else of __ioat_prep_pq_lock, passing pqres so that a validate operation is built. Those helpers return NULL if the ring has no space (prep_lock released) or, for the 16-source helper, if no SED entry can be allocated (prep_lock still held); on success they return a descriptor with prep_lock left held. The completion path sets bits in *pqres only on a validate failure.
note: checked prep.c:618-644 and the two helpers; same SED-failure lock behaviour as ioat_prep_pq.

name: ioat_prep_pqxor
prose: Precondition: src has src_cnt entries. Behaviour: it returns NULL if the channel has IOAT_CHAN_DOWN set or if src_cnt > MAX_SCF. Otherwise it zeroes the first src_cnt bytes of a stack coefficient table, sets pq[0] = pq[1] = dst, ORs DMA_PREP_PQ_DISABLE_Q into flags, and returns the result of __ioat_prep_pq16_lock if src_cnt_flags(src_cnt, flags) > 8, else of __ioat_prep_pq_lock (no validate result pointer). Those helpers return NULL if the ring has no space (prep_lock released) or, for the 16-source helper, if no SED entry can be allocated (prep_lock still held); on success they return a descriptor with prep_lock left held.
note: checked prep.c:646-670; the coefficient table is memset only up to src_cnt, the rest of scf[MAX_SCF] is uninitialised.

name: start_pending_queue
prose: Precondition: chan is an mmp_pdma_chan whose device is an mmp_pdma_device. Behaviour: if chan->idle is false it returns with no changes. If chain_pending is empty it calls mmp_pdma_free_phy(chan) and returns; that helper does nothing when chan->phy is NULL, and otherwise writes 0 to the channel's DRCMR register of that phy and clears phy->vchan and chan->phy under phy_lock; chan->idle is left unchanged. If chan->phy is NULL it calls lookup_phy(chan), which takes phy_lock and picks the first phy (by priority group) with no vchan, setting its vchan to chan, and returns it or NULL; on NULL start_pending_queue returns without moving anything. Otherwise it moves all of chain_pending to the tail of chain_running, programs the first moved descriptor's physical address with pdev->ops->write_next_addr(chan->phy, ...), calls enable_chan(chan->phy) and sets chan->idle to false. enable_chan returns without doing anything if phy->vchan is NULL; otherwise it writes DRCMR_MAPVLD | phy->idx to the DRCMR register, sets (if byte_align) or clears (otherwise) the DALGN bit for the phy, and ORs the ops' run_bits into the DCSR register.
note: checked mmp_pdma.c:453-494, 396-428, 430-447, 294-317. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (free_phy returns early when phy is NULL, line 436-437); round 2 RIGHT (DALGN bit cleared when byte_align is false); original RIGHT (return when lookup_phy finds nothing).

name: poly_store
prose: Precondition: buf holds count bytes (a NUL-terminated string from sysfs); the MQ DCR mapping ppc440spe_mq_dcr_host is valid. Behaviour: when CONFIG_440SP is defined the function returns -EINVAL immediately (the rest is unreachable in that configuration). Otherwise it returns -EINVAL if count is 0 or greater than 6; parses buf as a base-16 unsigned long with kstrtoul and returns the parse error if it fails; returns -EINVAL if the value has any bit set outside 0x1FF; and otherwise reads DCRN_MQ0_CFBHL, replaces the 8 bits at MQ0_CFBHL_POLY with the low 8 bits of the value (the 0x100 bit is dropped), writes the register back and returns count.
note: slice cut head; function is poly_store (ppc4xx/adma.c:4367-4395). Reviewer round 15 claim WRONG: lines 4372-4375 return -EINVAL under CONFIG_440SP; the old prose was right on that point.

name: st_fdma_prep_slave_sg
prose: Precondition: chan is an ST FDMA channel, sgl a DMA-mapped scatterlist with sg_len entries, direction DMA_MEM_TO_DEV or DMA_DEV_TO_MEM. Behaviour: it returns NULL if st_fdma_prep_common rejects the arguments (chan NULL, sg_len 0 or a non-slave direction, the last case after logging), or if sgl is NULL. It allocates a descriptor with sg_len nodes with st_fdma_alloc_desc, returning NULL after logging 'no memory for desc' if that fails. It marks the descriptor non-cyclic and, for each scatterlist entry, fills a hardware node: next points to the following node (the last wraps to the first), control carries the DREQ line, fill_hw_node sets the common fields, saddr (for DMA_MEM_TO_DEV) or daddr (otherwise) gets the entry's DMA address, and nbytes and generic.length get its DMA length. It sets the end-of-node interrupt bit on the last node and returns the result of vchan_tx_prep(&fchan->vchan, &fdesc->vdesc, flags).
note: slice cut head; function is st_fdma_prep_slave_sg (st_fdma.c:507-558). Old prose matches the code; the 'caller must not free' wording was dropped as not shown in the function.

name: d40_alloc_mask_set
prose: Precondition: phy is a physical channel resource with an initialised lock, first_user is writable; for logical allocation (is_log true) log_event_line is a valid bit index. Behaviour: under phy->lock (irqsave) it sets *first_user to true when (allocated_src | allocated_dst) equals D40_ALLOC_FREE. If is_log is false it requires both allocated_src and allocated_dst to be D40_ALLOC_FREE: then it sets both to D40_ALLOC_PHY and returns true; otherwise it changes nothing and returns false. If is_log is true it works on allocated_src when is_src is true and allocated_dst otherwise: it returns false if that mask is D40_ALLOC_PHY; converts D40_ALLOC_FREE to D40_ALLOC_LOG_FREE (0, a conversion that stays even if the call then fails); and, if the BIT(log_event_line) bit is clear, sets it and returns true, else returns false. The other mask is not touched in the logical case. The lock is released with interrupts restored on every path.
note: checked ste_dma40.c:1767-1819. Reviewer rounds 1 and 15 WRONG: the physical path requires both masks FREE and sets both to D40_ALLOC_PHY (lines 1779-1783).

name: stm32_dma_set_xfer_param
prose: Precondition: chan is an initialised channel with a valid dma_sconfig and threshold, buswidth is writable, direction is DMA_MEM_TO_DEV or DMA_DEV_TO_MEM, and buf_len and buf_addr describe the buffer. Behaviour: for DMA_MEM_TO_DEV it derives the destination (device) bus width and burst from dma_sconfig, sets chan->mem_width to the maximum memory width for the buffer, derives the memory bus width and a memory burst (1 if buf_addr is not aligned to buf_len, else STM32_DMA_MAX_BURST) and builds dma_scr; it updates the FIFO threshold field of chan->chan_reg.dma_sfcr (set from the threshold unless it is STM32_DMA_FIFO_THRESHOLD_NONE), sets dma_spar to the destination address and *buswidth to the destination width. DMA_DEV_TO_MEM is analogous with the source side as the device, and additionally stores the burst values in chan->mem_burst (twice) and sets chan->mem_width. A failing stm32_dma_get_width or stm32_dma_get_burst returns its negative error at that point, with chan->mem_width (and in DEV_TO_MEM chan->mem_burst) possibly already updated, chan->chan_reg.dma_sfcr, dma_spar and dma_scr not yet modified and *buswidth unwritten; any other direction logs and returns -EINVAL. After the switch it calls stm32_dma_set_fifo_config(chan, src_best_burst, dst_best_burst), clears the direction, size and burst fields of chan->chan_reg.dma_scr, ORs in the new dma_scr and returns 0.
note: checked stm32-dma.c:930-1075. Reviewer round 15 WRONG: stm32_dma_set_fifo_config is called at line 1066; rounds 1-2 RIGHT: mem_burst is only set in DEV_TO_MEM while mem_width is set in both. The clause 'apart from nothing' was removed: the dma_sfcr FTH update only happens after the width/burst lookups succeed.

name: stm32_dma3_chan_irq
prose: Precondition: devid is the stm32_dma3_chan, and the caller does not hold chan->vchan.lock; chan->swdesc is valid whenever a transfer-complete interrupt with TCIE enabled is reported. Behaviour: it takes chan->vchan.lock (spin_lock, not irqsave) and reads MISR; if the channel's MIS bit is clear it unlocks and returns IRQ_NONE with no other change. Otherwise it reads CSR and the enabled-interrupt bits of CCR; if TCF and TCIE are set it calls vchan_cyclic_callback for a cyclic descriptor or stm32_dma3_chan_complete otherwise; if USEF and USEIE are set it logs, sets chan->dma_status to DMA_ERROR, calls stm32_dma3_check_user_setting and stm32_dma3_chan_reset; if ULEF and ULEIE are set, or DTEF and DTEIE are set, it logs, sets DMA_ERROR and calls stm32_dma3_chan_reset. It then masks csr with (ccr | CCR_HTIE) and, if the result is nonzero, writes it to CFCR to clear those flags; it unlocks and returns IRQ_HANDLED.
note: slice cut head; real name is stm32_dma3_chan_irq (stm32-dma3.c:1006-1064); no stm32_dma3_chan_irq_handler. Checked each branch.

name: get_host_pd0
prose: Precondition: length is a u32. Behaviour: a pure function that returns (DESC_TYPE_HOST << DESC_TYPE) | length computed in u32, where DESC_TYPE_HOST is 0x10 and DESC_TYPE is 27, so the type contribution is 0x10 << 27 = 0x80000000 (bit 31). Any bits of length at bit 27 and above are OR-ed in unmasked (bit 31 is already set by the type). It has no side effects.
note: cppi41.c:17-18 (DESC_TYPE 27, DESC_TYPE_HOST 0x10) and 516-524. All three reviewer values were WRONG: the host type is 0x10 shifted by 27, giving 0x80000000, not 1<<26 or 2<<26.

name: edma_probe
prose: Precondition: pdev is the platform device for an EDMA3 controller with either an OF node or platform data. Behaviour: with an OF node it matches the binding, calls edma_setup_info_from_dt and returns its error (via PTR_ERR) if it fails; it returns -ENODEV if there is no info at all, the error from dma_set_mask_and_coherent(32 bits), -ENOMEM if the edma_cc allocation fails, -ENODEV if no memory resource exists (looked up as "edma3_cc" then index 0), and the error of devm_ioremap_resource; none of those paths has set the platform drvdata yet. It then sets the drvdata to ecc, enables runtime PM and calls pm_runtime_get_sync, on failure calling pm_runtime_disable and returning the error without a put. Later failures (edma_setup_from_hw, allocation of the slave/slot/mask arrays -> -ENOMEM, irq-name allocation -> -ENOMEM, devm_request_irq) go to err_disable_pm, which calls pm_runtime_put_sync and pm_runtime_disable and returns the error; failures after the dummy slot was allocated (a failed edma_alloc_slot returns its error to err_disable_pm; the tc_list allocation -> -ENOMEM, and the registration of the slave or memcpy dma_device) go to err_reg1, which frees the dummy slot and falls into err_disable_pm; if the memcpy registration fails the slave device is unregistered first. In the non-legacy path errors from of_parse_phandle_with_fixed_args stop the loop but are not returned. The OF DMA controller registration result is ignored. On success it returns 0 with the controller registered, runtime PM enabled and a runtime PM usage reference held; the drvdata remains set to ecc after any failure that came after platform_set_drvdata.
note: slice cut head; function is edma_probe (edma.c:2286-2554). Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (drvdata set only at line 2345, after the early returns).

name: udma_check_tx_completion
prose: Precondition: work is the tx_drain.work of a udma_chan, called from a workqueue where sleeping is allowed, with uc->vc.lock not held. Behaviour: it loops: it takes uc->vc.lock (irqsave); if uc->desc is non-NULL it saves the previous tx_drain residue and timestamp and sets desc_done from udma_is_desc_really_done (which refreshes the tx_drain residue and timestamp for a PDMA TX channel); desc_done keeps its old value (true on the first pass) when uc->desc is NULL. If desc_done is false it computes the time and residue differences since the previous poll; if the residue changed it unlocks, sleeps for a delay derived from the drain rate with usleep_range and loops again; if it did not change it schedules tx_drain.work again after HZ (one second) and leaves the loop. If desc_done is true and uc->desc is non-NULL it decrements the byte counters by d->residue, calls udma_start and vchan_cookie_complete and leaves the loop; if uc->desc is NULL it leaves the loop. The lock is released with the saved flags on every exit from the loop. If uc->desc becomes NULL during a sleep, desc_done stays false and the next pass reuses the stale residue and time values, so the outcome (another sleep or a one-second reschedule) depends on the stale difference rather than being necessarily a reschedule.
note: checked k3-udma.c:1086-1153. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (residue_diff/time_diff are stale when desc is NULL after a sleep, so it may sleep and loop again); round 2 and original RIGHT.

name: f1x_lookup_addr_in_dct
prose: Precondition: nid is a node id for edac_mc_find and in_addr and dct select the system address and DCT to search. Behaviour: it returns -EINVAL if edac_mc_find(nid) finds no memory controller. Otherwise, for each chip-select row of the DCT that is enabled (csrow_enabled), it fetches the base and mask with get_cs_base_and_mask and compares (in_addr & ~mask) with (base & ~mask); on the first match it stops and returns that row if the family is 0x15 with model 0x30 or later, or else the value of f10_process_possible_spare, which returns the row, or the first row whose base has bit 0x2 set when the online-spare swap is done and the matched row is the bad DRAM chip select. If no enabled row matches it returns -EINVAL. It takes no locks of its own.
note: checked amd64_edac.c:2214-2256 and f10_process_possible_spare (2189-2204). Old prose fine; added the family-0x15 shortcut and the -EINVAL for no match. Contract left empty because the function reads device state.

name: i82975x_init
prose: Precondition: called once at module load. Behaviour: it calls opstate_init, then pci_register_driver(&i82975x_driver) and, if that returns a negative value, goes to fail0 which calls pci_dev_put(mci_pdev) and returns that value (during registration the probe may already have set mci_pdev through i82975x_init_one, which takes a reference with pci_dev_get when mci_pdev is NULL). If registration succeeded and mci_pdev is still NULL it finds the Intel 82975_0 device with pci_get_device (storing the referenced device in mci_pdev), going to fail1 with -ENODEV if none exists, and otherwise calls i82975x_init_one on it, going to fail1 with -ENODEV (replacing the original error) if that returns a negative value. fail1 unregisters the driver and falls into fail0, which calls pci_dev_put(mci_pdev), leaving the mci_pdev pointer itself unchanged. It returns 0 if mci_pdev was already set after registration or the init_one succeeded.
note: checked i82975x_edac.c:644-684 and the pci_dev_get at line 601-602. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (the probe path through pci_register_driver can set mci_pdev, so pci_get_device may be skipped); round 2 RIGHT (init_one takes no extra reference on the pci_get_device path).

name: EDAC_SCRUB_ATTR_SHOW(addr, read_addr, u64, "0x%llx\n")
prose: Generated function addr_show(ras_feat_dev, attr, buf), expanded from EDAC_SCRUB_ATTR_SHOW(addr, read_addr, u64, "0x%llx\n"). Precondition: the attribute is a scrub attribute whose instance indexes a valid ctx->scrub[inst] with non-NULL scrub_ops and a non-NULL read_addr callback, and buf is the sysfs page buffer. Behaviour: it calls ops->read_addr(parent device, private, &data); if that returns nonzero it returns that value, otherwise it returns the result of sysfs_emit(buf, "0x%llx\n", data), normally the number of bytes written, or a negative error from sysfs_emit if buf is not page aligned.
note: scrub.c:38-55. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: sysfs_emit can return -EINVAL for an unaligned buffer (not shown in the function).

name: skx_init
prose: Precondition: called once at module load; it inspects global state itself. Behaviour: it returns -EBUSY if ghes_get_devices() is nonzero or another EDAC owner than this module exists, and -ENODEV if running under a hypervisor or if the CPU is not in skx_cpuids. It then stores the res_config, reads the top-of-memory registers with skx_get_hi_lo and returns its error directly (nothing to undo yet). It then calls skx_get_all_bus_mappings: a negative result goes to the fail label; a zero result returns -ENODEV without calling skx_remove; a positive result is the socket count. For each entry of skx_all_munits it calls get_all_munits (negative goes to fail; a count differing from per_socket * sockets sets -ENODEV and goes to fail), then for each socket reads the source id with skx_get_src_id (negative goes to fail) and registers each of its memory controllers with skx_register_mci (negative goes to fail). Success continues with skx_set_decode, the optional ADXL decode setup when nvdimm_count is nonzero, opstate_init, skx_setup_debug("skx_test") and mce_register_decode_chain, and returns 0. The fail label calls skx_remove and returns rc, so cleanup also happens when skx_get_all_bus_mappings itself returns a negative value.
note: checked skx_base.c:561-695. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: the fail label is reached from the first negative skx_get_all_bus_mappings result (line 590-591); the old prose said only after controllers were found.

name: iso_resource_work
prose: Precondition: work is the delayed work of an iso_resource r with a client reference held by this work item. Behaviour: under client->lock it reads the bus generation and r->todo, and, when todo is ISO_RES_ALLOC and the last bus reset was less than one second ago, reschedules itself after 333 ms and sets skip; otherwise skip is set for ISO_RES_REALLOC when r->generation already equals the current generation. It sets free for ISO_RES_DEALLOC, ISO_RES_ALLOC_ONCE and ISO_RES_DEALLOC_ONCE, and stores the generation in r->generation (also in the skip case). If skip it jumps to out. Otherwise it calls fw_iso_resource_manage; if the channel result is -EAGAIN for an ALLOC or REALLOC request it jumps to out (no event, no free). It computes success (channel >= 0 or bandwidth > 0). Under the lock, if r->todo is still ISO_RES_ALLOC it becomes ISO_RES_REALLOC, and if r->todo is ISO_RES_REALLOC, success is false, the client is not shutting down and xa_erase removes the resource, it drops one extra client reference and sets free. For todo == ISO_RES_ALLOC and channel >= 0 it stores 1 << channel in r->channels. For ISO_RES_REALLOC with success it jumps to out without queueing an event. Otherwise it takes the e_alloc event (todo ISO_RES_ALLOC or ISO_RES_ALLOC_ONCE) or the e_dealloc event (all other todos, including a failed REALLOC), fills in the handle, channel and bandwidth and queues it with queue_event (the queued event buffer is owned by the client queue afterwards). If free is set it cancels the delayed work and kfree's r->e_alloc and r->e_dealloc (only the buffer not used for the queued event is still non-NULL) and r. The out label always drops one client reference.
note: checked core-cdev.c:1317-1409. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: the queued event is not freed here (its pointer was set to NULL before kfree); rounds 1 and 2 RIGHT (skip/EAGAIN return silently, REALLOC success returns silently); the old prose also said the ALLOC skip returns 'within one second of the last reset' which matches line 1330-1333.

name: ffa_memory_attributes_get
prose: Precondition: none; func_id is a 32-bit function id. Behaviour: a pure function returning u16. It returns 0 if func_id equals FFA_FN_NATIVE(MEM_LEND) or FFA_MEM_LEND, and otherwise returns FFA_MEM_NORMAL | FFA_MEM_WRITE_BACK | FFA_MEM_INNER_SHAREABLE, which is BIT(5) | (3 << 2) | 3 = 0x2F. It reads only func_id and has no side effects.
note: slice cut head; function is ffa_memory_attributes_get (arm_ffa/driver.c:665-675). Constants checked in include/linux/arm_ffa.h: FFA_MEM_LEND is FFA_SMC_32(0x72), not 0x84000001, and the attribute value is 0x2F, not 0x7, so the old prose was wrong on both.

name: scmi_clock_state_get
prose: Precondition: ph is a protocol handle whose private data holds the clock_info; enabled should point to a writable bool. Behaviour: it performs no clock-domain lookup and no NULL check of its own; it returns the result of ci->clock_config_get(ph, clk_id, NULL_OEM_TYPE, NULL, enabled, NULL, atomic), the clock config getter installed for the protocol version. For the version installed as scmi_clock_config_get it returns -EINVAL if enabled is NULL and otherwise performs a CLOCK_ATTRIBUTES transfer, setting *enabled on success; the version scmi_clock_config_get_v2 accepts a NULL enabled and only writes it on success. The result is 0 on success or a negative error from the transfer setup or transfer.
note: checked clock.c:866-873, 836-864 (scmi_clock_config_get), and the v2 getter above it. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: the NULL check is in the callee, not in this function, and the v2 callee accepts NULL; round 2 RIGHT (no clk_id lookup).

name: scmi_powercap_validate
prose: Precondition: none. Behaviour: a pure function. It returns -EPROTO if min_val or max_val is 0; -EPROTO if configurable is true and min_val equals max_val, or if configurable is false and min_val differs from max_val; -EPROTO if min_val differs from max_val and step_val is 0; and 0 otherwise. No other value is returned and nothing is modified.
note: powercap.c:177-192. Contract left empty because the return is an errno name.

name: sdei_to_linux_errno
prose: Precondition: none; sdei_err is an unsigned long firmware status. Behaviour: a pure switch with no side effects: SDEI_NOT_SUPPORTED (-1) gives -EOPNOTSUPP, SDEI_INVALID_PARAMETERS (-2) gives -EINVAL, SDEI_DENIED (-3) gives -EPERM, SDEI_PENDING (-5) gives -EINPROGRESS, SDEI_OUT_OF_RESOURCE (-10) gives -ENOMEM, and every other value, including SDEI_SUCCESS, gives 0.
note: arm_sdei.c:118-134, constants in include/uapi/linux/arm_sdei.h:41-45. Contract left empty because the prose lists errno names.

name: NVRAM_READ_VAL(u8)
prose: Generated function nvram_read_u8(prefix, postfix, name, val, allset, fallback), expanded from NVRAM_READ_VAL(u8). Precondition: name is a NUL-terminated string, prefix and postfix are NUL-terminated or NULL, val is writable. Behaviour: it looks the variable up with get_nvram_var (which, when fallback is set and the first lookup returns -ENOENT with a prefix, retries without the prefix) and returns without changes if the lookup returns a negative value. It trims the value with strim and parses it with kstrtou8 (base 0); if parsing fails it logs a warning that names the variable, the value and the error and returns without changing *val. If allset is nonzero and the parsed value equals allset it returns without changing *val. Otherwise it stores the value in *val. It returns nothing.
note: bcm47xx_sprom.c:65-89. Reviewer round 15 RIGHT: the parse-failure path logs a warning (pr_warn), so the function can have another effect.

name: cper_print_proc_arm
prose: Precondition: proc points to a CPER ARM processor error section whose section_length is trusted only as checked below, length is the size of the CPER record buffer, pfx is a NUL-terminated prefix. Behaviour: it prints the MIDR, then computes len = section_length - (sizeof(*proc) + err_info_num * sizeof(error info)); if len is negative or section_length exceeds length it prints diagnostics ("too small" or "too big") and returns without printing anything else. Otherwise it prints MPIDR, affinity level and running/PSCI state according to proc->validation_bits, then for each of the err_info_num error-info structures prints the error count, the flags selected by its validation bits, the error type (noting reserved bits), error_info (also decoded with cper_print_arm_err_info), virtual fault address and physical fault address as flagged. It then walks the context-info structures: for each it prints the index, computes the 16-byte-aligned size (reading ctx_info->size before checking it against len), and returns after printing 'section length is too small' and 'firmware-generated error record is incorrect' if the size exceeds the remaining len, or after printing 'Invalid context type' if the type is above the table maximum; otherwise it prints the register context type, hex-dumps its data, subtracts the size from len and advances. If len is still positive afterwards it hex-dumps the remaining bytes as vendor-specific error info. It returns nothing and allocates nothing.
note: slice cut head; real name is cper_print_proc_arm (cper-arm.c:248-345). Old prose omitted the up-front MIDR print and the early return on a bad section_length (lines 249-262).

name: efi_earlycon_write
prose: Precondition: the font and screen_info (lfb_width, lfb_height, lfb_linelength) are set up, the cursor globals efi_x, efi_y, cur_line_y, max_line_y are initialised, and str holds num bytes. Behaviour: it returns nothing. It repeatedly takes a chunk of text up to the next newline, limited to what fits on the current line, and draws it scanline by scanline: for each of the font->height scanlines it maps the framebuffer line with efi_earlycon_map and returns from the whole function immediately if the map returns NULL (leaving the rest of str undrawn, earlier scanlines of the chunk possibly drawn, and efi_x and efi_y not yet advanced for the chunk); it unmaps each line after drawing it. After a chunk it advances num, str and efi_x; if the next character is a newline it consumes it and moves to the start of the next text line (efi_x = 0, efi_y += font->height), and it does the same wrap if the next glyph would pass the right edge. If the next line would exceed lfb_height it records the cursor x in efi_x_array[cur_line_y], advances cur_line_y modulo max_line_y, lowers efi_y by one text row, calls efi_earlycon_scroll_up and clears the last text row's scanlines with efi_earlycon_clear_scanline; a map failure inside scroll_up or clear_scanline only ends that helper, not efi_earlycon_write. Every successful mapping is unmapped before moving on.
note: slice cut head; function is efi_earlycon_write (earlycon.c:145-216). Reviewer round 15 RIGHT (helpers return on their own map failure, lines 107-114); round 2 RIGHT on newline vs space and the unchanged cursor on map failure.

name: efi_init
prose: Precondition: called once during early boot on an architecture using the FDT UEFI parameters. Behaviour: it calls efi_get_fdt_params(&data), which returns the EFI system table address (a u64, 0 meaning no UEFI information), and returns immediately if that is 0. It calls efi_memmap_init_early and panics if it returns a negative value; warns if the memory descriptor version is not 1. If uefi_init(efi_system_table) returns a negative value it calls efi_memmap_unmap and returns without further setup. Otherwise it calls reserve_regions, early_init_dt_check_for_usable_mem_range, efi_find_mirror, efi_esrt_init and efi_mokvar_table_init, reserves the memory-map pages with memblock_reserve, and, if CONFIG_X86, CONFIG_SYSFB or CONFIG_EFI_EARLYCON is enabled, calls init_screen_info. It returns nothing and leaves the memory map mapped on the success path.
note: slice cut head; function is efi_init (efi-init.c:233-278). Reviewer round 15 claim WRONG: efi_get_fdt_params returns the u64 table address and 0 means failure (line 239-241), not a negative value.

name: efi_random_get_seed
prose: Precondition: EFI boot services and variable services are callable. Behaviour: it locates the EFI RNG protocol (on failure the RNG seed size is 0 and the failing status is remembered) and reads the size of the "RandomSeed" variable; if neither the RNG nor a variable is available it returns that locate_protocol status immediately, before any allocation and before looking at a bootloader table. Otherwise it looks for an existing LINUX_EFI_RANDOM_SEED_TABLE_GUID table, using it only if its size is at most 512 (a smaller-or-zero or larger table is ignored), and allocates a pool buffer for the combined size, going to err_warn (returning the allocate_pool status, without freeing) if that fails. It fills it with EFI_RANDOM_SEED_SIZE bytes from GetRng (raw algorithm, falling back to any algorithm on EFI_UNSUPPORTED), and then with the "RandomSeed" variable, which counts only if both reading and deleting it succeed (otherwise that region is zeroed). If no bytes were obtained it frees (after zeroing) the buffer and returns the last status. Otherwise it appends the used previous table bytes, sets the size and installs the buffer with install_configuration_table; on failure it zeroes and frees the buffer and returns that status, leaving the old table in place. On success it zeroes and frees the previous table only if its bytes were used (size at most 512 and nonzero), and returns EFI_SUCCESS. Failures of GetRng or of the variable steps are ignored when other bytes were obtained.
note: checked libstub/random.c:65-179 (slice cut head). Reviewer round 15 claim WRONG: with neither RNG nor variable the function returns at line 82-83 before get_efi_config_table is called; round 1 RIGHT (set_efi_var failure does not by itself fail the function when bytes exist).

name: riscv_enable_runtime_services
prose: Precondition: runs once as an early initcall after the EFI boot state and memory map are initialised. Behaviour: it returns 0 (after a message) if EFI_BOOT is not enabled. Otherwise it unmaps the early memory map and remaps it with efi_memmap_init_late(efi.memmap.phys_map, desc_size * nr_map); if that fails it prints an error and returns 0. If efi_soft_reserve_enabled() it walks the memory descriptors and, for each with EFI_MEMORY_SP, kzallocs a 'Soft Reserved' IORESOURCE_MEM resource (IORES_DESC_SOFT_RESERVED) and inserts it into iomem_resource; if kzalloc fails it WARNs and stops the walk, keeping the already-inserted resources. It then returns 0 if efi_runtime_disabled() or if EFI_RUNTIME_SERVICES is already set in efi.flags. Otherwise it calls efi_virtmap_init; if that returns false it logs an error and returns -ENOMEM (the soft-reserve work stays done); if it returns true it calls efi_native_runtime_setup, sets EFI_RUNTIME_SERVICES in efi.flags and returns 0.
note: checked riscv-runtime.c:66-130. Reviewer rounds 2 and 15 RIGHT: a kzalloc failure only stops the soft-reserve loop, it does not fix the final return value, which is still -ENOMEM if efi_virtmap_init fails.

name: gsmi_exec
prose: Precondition: gsmi_dev.param_buf, smi_cmd and handshake_type are set up; func and sub are the command bytes. The function itself takes no lock and shares gsmi_dev's buffer, so concurrent callers must serialise externally. Behaviour: it builds cmd = (sub << 8) | func and triggers the SMI with inline assembly using the configured handshake (set carry and wait for the handler to clear it for GSMI_HANDSHAKE_CF, spin spincount iterations after the outb for GSMI_HANDSHAKE_SPIN, or only the outb for GSMI_HANDSHAKE_NONE), reading the status from AX. It then maps the status: GSMI_SUCCESS to 0; GSMI_VAR_NOT_FOUND to 1; invalid parameter to -EINVAL; buffer too small to -ENOMEM; GSMI_UNSUPPORTED and GSMI_UNSUPPORTED2 to -ENOSYS (logged unless sub is the handshake-type command); not ready to -EBUSY; GSMI_DEVICE_ERROR to -EFAULT; GSMI_NOT_FOUND to -ENOENT; GSMI_LOG_FULL to -ENOSPC; the three handshake codes GSMI_HANDSHAKE_SPIN, GSMI_HANDSHAKE_CF and GSMI_HANDSHAKE_NONE (0x7d, 0x7e, 0x7f) are returned unchanged as the result; any other status logs an unknown-error message and gives -ENXIO.
note: gsmi.c:190-304. Old prose was wrong on the handshake status values (they are 0x7d-0x7f, not 10-12); reviewer round 1 only partially RIGHT: the function does not take the lock, which matches the old wording, but callers are not verified here.

name: imx_sc_to_linux_errno
prose: Precondition: none; errno may be any int. Behaviour: a pure lookup with no side effects: if 0 <= errno < IMX_SC_ERR_LAST (12) it returns imx_sc_linux_errmap[errno], namely 0, -EINVAL, -EINVAL, -EINVAL, -EACCES, -EACCES, -ERANGE, -EEXIST, -EPERM, -EPIPE, -EBUSY, -EIO for errno 0 to 11; for any other value it returns -EIO.
note: imx-scu.c:68-91; errno numbers: ERANGE 34, EEXIST 17, EPERM 1, EPIPE 32, EBUSY 16, EIO 5. Contract left empty because the prose names errno values.

name: psci_to_linux_errno
prose: Precondition: errno is a PSCI firmware status. Behaviour: a pure switch with no side effects: PSCI_RET_SUCCESS (0) gives 0, PSCI_RET_NOT_SUPPORTED (-1) gives -EOPNOTSUPP, PSCI_RET_INVALID_PARAMS (-2) and PSCI_RET_INVALID_ADDRESS (-9) give -EINVAL, PSCI_RET_DENIED (-3) gives -EPERM, and every other value gives -EINVAL.
note: psci.c:135-149 and include/uapi/linux/psci.h:131-140. Old prose gave the wrong numeric values for DENIED (-3, not -4) and INVALID_ADDRESS (-9, not -3); contract left empty because the prose names errno values.

name: psci_set_osi_mode
prose: Precondition: PSCI 1.0 firmware with SET_SUSPEND_MODE support is assumed. Behaviour: it calls invoke_psci_fn(PSCI_1_0_FN_SET_SUSPEND_MODE) with PSCI_1_0_SUSPEND_MODE_OSI if enable is true, else PSCI_1_0_SUSPEND_MODE_PC; if the firmware status is negative it logs a firmware-bug message naming the mode and the status. It returns psci_to_linux_errno of the status (0, -EOPNOTSUPP, -EINVAL or -EPERM).

name: __psci_cpu_suspend
prose: Precondition: the PSCI conduit (invoke_psci_fn) has been set up. Behaviour: it calls invoke_psci_fn(fn, state, entry_point, 0). It then returns psci_to_linux_errno of the firmware's return value: 0 for PSCI_RET_SUCCESS, -EOPNOTSUPP for PSCI_RET_NOT_SUPPORTED, -EINVAL for PSCI_RET_INVALID_PARAMS, PSCI_RET_INVALID_ADDRESS or any unrecognised status, and -EPERM for PSCI_RET_DENIED. It takes no locks and has no other effects on kernel state.
note: psci.c:135-275; psci_to_linux_errno maps the firmware status as above (PSCI_RET_DENIED is -3 and PSCI_RET_INVALID_ADDRESS is -9 in include/uapi/linux/psci.h).
